angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 381,939 km at 117.55 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.5067 +/- 0.0193 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 117.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.549 +/- 0.024 solar radii from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-323 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract): 381,939 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.478 +/- 0.089 solar masses from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-323 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3710 +/- 118 K from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-323 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-323 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-323.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.638, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
